newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan jobless graduates go on hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan jobless graduates go on hunger strike.

text.p: More than 1,200 jobless graduates have gone on indefinite hunger strike after the authorities prevented a demonstration they planned outside parliament last week to push for jobs, a spokesman for the group said on Monday.

"The authorities gave the order to crush the march just as we were about to leave the union headquarters where we had been staging a sit-in since October 25," the spokesman for the Association of Jobless Graduates said.

Representatives of the jobless graduates had met government officials on Friday after a two-day hunger strike. The spokesman said officials had agreed to remove police from around the union headquarters to lay the groundwork for what they termed "fair talks".
"We were amazed to see that police were still there and decided to stage our scheduled march," he added.
Officials at the interior ministry were not immediately available to comment.

Last May, an estimated 2,000 jobless graduates went on a three-week sit-in and hunger strike at the headquarters of the Moroccan Labour Union (UMT) in protest against what they said was the government's failure to provide them with jobs.
